title: Understanding SVD Output
text: When you perform Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) on a matrix, you decompose it into three matrices: U, Σ (Sigma), and $$V^T$$. Each of these matrices has specific dimensions based on the original matrix. Consider how the dimensions of these matrices relate to the original matrix.

title: Dimensions of U and Σ
text: The matrix U from the SVD has the same number of rows as the original matrix. The diagonal matrix Σ contains the singular values and its dimensions are determined by the rank of the original matrix. Think about how these dimensions affect the product U times Σ.

title: Calculating the Shape of U times Σ
text: Given that U has dimensions $$(940,7)$$ and Σ is a diagonal matrix with dimensions $$(7,7)$$, what would be the resulting dimensions of the product U times Σ?
